author: WP16
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on sharp-runtime's real object model: opt-in Object, String as a static vocabulary, exceptions under std::exception, RAII-first lifetime and GC stubs, three delegate representations and RTTI-only Type/Activator. Mostly current at sharp-runtime next @ 41b918c9; stale details are the Object subclass count, Delegate equality, Activator overloads and DateTime::Now(). The site had only the IDisposable pattern (Tutorial 89) and the event token idiom; the full model is now on the object-model deep dive.

concepts.text: sharp-runtime keeps .NET names but its object model is standard C++: values, explicit interfaces, RAII, smart pointers where identity matters, and RTTI for the little type identity that survives.
System::Object is abstract (pure virtual GetTypeName) and exactly three sharp-runtime classes derive from it: DateTime, DateTimeOffset and Timers::Timer.
Object::Equals(const Object*) is pointer identity; static Equals handles nulls then dispatches; ReferenceEquals is strict pointer equality.
GetHashCode() hashes the address masked with 0x7fffffff (non-negative); ToString() returns GetTypeName(); non-virtual GetType() uses typeid(*this), reporting the most-derived type.
The GetTypeName macros only remove boilerplate; they are not a hidden registration system and do not make Object universal.
CNA's XNA layer is the opposite: 63 class declarations in CNA public headers derive from System::Object because its porting checklist requires GetTypeName overrides.

concepts.section: String is an API vocabulary, not storage
concepts.text: System::String has deleted constructor and destructor; its static methods take and return std::string, the real value type (SharpRuntime::String).

concepts.section: String is an API vocabulary, not storage
concepts.text: A std::string is never null, so String::IsNullOrEmpty only tests emptiness; code distinguishing null from empty keeps that state separately, e.g. std::optional<std::string>.

concepts.section: String is an API vocabulary, not storage
concepts.text: StringBuilder is a real mutable buffer over one std::string; its chunk enumerator keeps .NET's shape but yields one chunk.
System::Exception derives from std::exception and keeps message, inner exception, Data, Source, HelpLink and HResult (0x80131500, COR_E_EXCEPTION); what() exposes the message.
StackTrace is empty (no managed stack); GetBaseException() is absent because returning a base value slices; TargetSite and GetObjectData are absent (reflection, serialization).
There is no central ThrowHelper: each method throws its specific type, so parity includes the class and message at each site.
System::GC cannot collect: mutating calls are no-ops and queries return documented constants rather than heap statistics.
Value types use value semantics, shared_ptr where reference identity matters, unique_ptr for exclusive ownership; no project smart pointer or tracing heap.
tokens: no project-specific smart pointer or tracing heap

concepts.text: IDisposable implementations release deterministically, should not generally throw and tolerate repeated calls; it does not replace destructors.
Destructors are implicitly noexcept, so an I/O failure escaping during unwinding terminates; explicit Dispose()/Close() is where failures are observed.
concepts.note: The claim that audit work fixed 'several' destructor paths was not counted and is not published.

concepts.text: Most delegate-shaped declarations are std::function aliases: one target, no multicast equality, no late binding.

System::Delegate stores one erased void() callable or an invocation list and implements Combine, Remove, RemoveAll, ordered Invoke and GetInvocationList; equality is by plain function pointer where possible, a closure equals only itself.
concepts.note: Bible: entry equality is pointer identity.

concepts.text: A single-target Delegate must already be owned by shared_ptr before GetInvocationList() returns itself, otherwise std::bad_weak_ptr.
Delegate::DynamicInvoke always throws NotImplementedException because C++ has no reflection-driven object[] invocation.
MulticastAction is the event-field alternative (tokens, snapshot invocation) and EventHandler<T> adds sender/argument shape and a replay hook; neither makes every std::function multicast.
Type::From<T>() with RTTI-backed equality gives genuine identity for keys, registries and equality tests, but not CLR metadata; predicates are placeholders and must not be branched on.

Activator::CreateInstance<T>() default-constructs a compile-time type; runtime Type, assembly-name and argument-array overloads are absent, while a compile-time variadic CreateInstance<T>(args...) exists.
concepts.note: Bible: argument-array overloads absent without mentioning the compile-time variadic form.

concepts.text: Every surviving mechanism has a clear C++ owner: RTTI for identity, templates for construction, smart pointers for shared lifetime, interfaces for capabilities.
